{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeACqbw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHhSao", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 265, "title": "Support reusable subgraphs with automatic synchronization across referencing graphs", "body": "## Goal

Allow users to define a reusable **subgraph** once and insert it into multiple graphs as a single node. When the subgraph is edited and saved, **all referencing graphs automatically use its latest saved definition**. The purpose is to reuse shared processing (e.g. ASR pipeline) while letting each parent graph keep its own concrete input and output nodes (microphone vs tab audio, text window vs focused field).

**Approved direction:** Keep concrete Input/Output nodes, graph controls and relevant event handling **inside the existing Graph Editor**. Do **not** introduce separate run-trigger/event/binding setup or graph-wide abstract external Input/Output settings as part of this feature.

## Minimal UI/UX changes

1. **Graph Library**: show regular graphs and reusable subgraphs together in the **existing library**, with a simple way to distinguish/filter their type. No separate subgraph library, sidebar, dashboard, folders, activity history, or extra screens.
2. **Graph Editor**: select a group of connected nodes and choose **Create Subgraph**. The selected nodes are extracted into a reusable definition and replaced by one subgraph node; infer its exposed input/output ports from connections crossing the selection boundary. Ensure the user can review/edit meaningful port names without an unrelated configuration system.
3. **Edit a subgraph** using the **same existing Graph Editor canvas**. Open it from its instance (e.g. double-click or an explicit Edit action) and provide a simple way back to the parent graph. It can also be opened directly from Graph Library.
4. **Add Node**: include saved subgraphs in the existing node picker. Each instance has typed ports and can be wired like an ordinary node.
5. Avoid all unrelated or speculative UI additions. Preserve current graph management, editing and launch UX unless required for subgraphs.

## Shared-definition semantics and sync

- Each reusable subgraph has one persistent, stable identity and saved definition. Instances in parent graphs **reference that identity**, rather than embedding detached copies.
- **Saving** a subgraph updates the shared definition; every dependent graph resolves the **new definition automatically**, including nested references if supported. **No manual sync, reimport, relink, or per-instance update step.**
- **Running sessions keep their already-started snapshot**; changes take effect for subsequent executions, not as a destructive hot swap of active sessions.
- An unchanged parent graph should not need manual re-save to pick up the updated subgraph. Across tabs/windows, stored revisions and editor views should remain consistent.
- Preserve a usable external port contract. If an edit removes or changes an exposed port/type and would break parents, surface affected references clearly **before committing** and prevent an unnoticed broken configuration; define a safe, explicit migration or resolution mechanism.
- Handle renaming, duplication, deletion, import/export, external storage changes and stale editors without dangling references or silent data loss. Deletion of a referenced subgraph should be blocked or require an explicit safe resolution, never silently destroy dependent graphs.
- Detect invalid/circular subgraph references; avoid infinite recursion and provide actionable errors.
- Keep graph validation, typed-port compatibility, model requirements, worker/runtime cleanup, current graph persistence, and Live/Web independence intact.

## Test scenarios / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build a reusable processing chain in the existing editor via **Create Subgraph**; see it in the same Graph Library; insert it through **Add Node** into two different graphs.
- [ ] Example parents: `MicrophoneAudio → [Shared ASR Subgraph] → Text Output` and `ChromeTabAudio → [Shared ASR Subgraph] → Text Output`, without duplicating the ASR processing definition.
- [ ] Change an internal ASR node setting inside the shared subgraph and save. **Both parent graphs use the new setting on their next run without manual edits**; already-running sessions are not modified.
- [ ] Subgraph edits, port changes, errors and stale editor state behave safely and predictably (no silent broken connections or overwritten changes).
- [ ] Type validation works across subgraph boundaries; nested references and cycles are either supported safely or rejected with a clear explanation.
- [ ] Graph Library and Graph Editor reuse existing screens, with accessible keyboard actions and a way to navigate into/out of the subgraph; no new dedicated library or editor screen.
- [ ] Import/export and storage persistence preserve shared references with a documented strategy for missing dependencies and cross-install transfers.
- [ ] Regression tests cover graph editing, persistence, concurrent Live/Web execution, resolved model requirements and resource cleanup. Record tests run and any remaining limitations.

## Out of scope

- Graph-wide Trigger / Event / Input / Output binding architecture or Launch Settings redesign.
- New context menus, dashboards, templates, account controls, or other UI not essential to reusable subgraphs.
- Changing the current microphone permission/runtime flow (#263) or Graph Library navigation refactor (#260).
